`lf task run` creates a new Task worktree from the exact current canonical-main commit even when that commit is ahead of or otherwise unpublished to origin. Placement records that commit as the Task/PR base and leaves publication/rebase to the normal Task lifecycle.

* In a temporary repository whose clean canonical main is one or more commits ahead of origin/main, `lf task run` creates the sibling Task worktree and bases it at the exact local canonical-main HEAD.
* No push, reset, force-push, origin equality check, allowlist, or manual reconciliation is required.
* Existing Task/worktree reuse remains idempotent.
* Landing still rebases/integrates through normal Loopflow PR mechanics.
* A newly authorized configured Task can be created from clean, unpublished canonical main without first publishing Wave commits; do not reopen completed LOO-256.

This intentionally supersedes LOO-175’s fixed fetched-origin placement precondition while preserving its minimal-PR-range outcome. Remove the fixed-context precondition rather than extend it. Do not silently include uncommitted filesystem changes, mutate origin, or weaken Task/worktree ownership.
